# 1. Define the Master Crosswalk (Sex by Age Universe)

```{python}
# Path to the cached master file
csv_path = Path("intermediate/Utah_Census_All_Counties_All_Ages_2000_2023.csv")

if not csv_path.exists():
    print("Fetching universe data using Crosswalk...")
    data_frames = []

    # Iterate through target years
    for year in [2000, 2010, 2020] + list(range(2009, 2024)):
        try:
            # 1. Determine Dataset & Select Codes from Crosswalk
            if year in [2000, 2010]:
                dataset = "dec/sf1"
                codes = var_crosswalk["SF1"].tolist()
            elif year == 2020:
                dataset = "dec/dhc"
                codes = var_crosswalk["DHC"].tolist()
            else:
                dataset = "acs/acs5"
                codes = var_crosswalk["ACS"].tolist()

            # 2. Fetch Data (Requesting 'NAME' + All Codes)
            # We use the crosswalk codes to query the API
            df = get_census(
                dataset=dataset,
                variables=["NAME"] + codes,
                year=year,
                params={"for": "county:*", "in": "state:49"},
                return_geoid=False,
            )

            # 3. Rename Columns to Human-Readable Labels
            # Create map: {'P012003': 'Male: Under 5 years', ...}
            code_map = dict(zip(codes, var_crosswalk["Label"]))

            # Apply Rename
            # Also normalize 'NAME' to ensure consistency
            if "NAME" not in df.columns:
                # Attempt to find lowercase 'name' or warn
                col_name = next((c for c in df.columns if c.upper() == "NAME"), None)
                if col_name:
                    df = df.rename(columns={col_name: "NAME"})

            df_clean = df.rename(columns=code_map)

            # 4. Filter to keep only relevant columns (NAME + Label Columns)
            # This drops the 'state', 'county' FIPS columns usually returned by API
            keep_cols = ["NAME"] + var_crosswalk["Label"].tolist()

            # Intersection check to be safe (in case API didn't return a specific var)
            final_cols = [c for c in keep_cols if c in df_clean.columns]
            df_final = df_clean[final_cols].copy()

            df_final["Year"] = year
            df_final["Dataset"] = dataset

            data_frames.append(df_final)
            print(f"Fetched {year}")

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Skipping {year}: {e}")

    # Save to CSV
    if data_frames:
        df_master = pd.concat(data_frames, ignore_index=True)
        csv_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        df_master.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Master file saved: {csv_path}")
```

```{python}
# 1. Load Master File
df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)

# 2. Filter Geography (Wasatch Front)
wftdm_counties = [
    "Box Elder County",
    "Weber County",
    "Davis County",
    "Salt Lake County",
    "Utah County",
]
df["Geography"] = df["NAME"].str.split(",").str[0]
df_wfrc = df[df["Geography"].isin(wftdm_counties)].copy()

# 3. Filter Variables (18-24 Age Group)
# Since we have clean names, we can just search for the strings!
# We look for "18 and 19", "20", "21", "22 to 24"
# This avoids accidentally grabbing "Under 18" or "65"
target_keywords = ["18 and 19", "20 years", "21 years", "22 to 24"]

# Find columns that match these keywords
target_cols = [
    c
    for c in df_wfrc.columns
    if any(k in c for k in target_keywords) and "Male" in c or "Female" in c
]

# 4. Aggregate
for col in target_cols:
    df_wfrc[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_wfrc[col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)

df_wfrc["Population_18_24"] = df_wfrc[target_cols].sum(axis=1)

# 5. Pivot
df_census_college_age = (
    df_wfrc.pivot_table(
        index="Year", columns="Geography", values="Population_18_24", aggfunc="sum"
    )
    .reset_index()
    .rename_axis(None, axis=1)
)

print("Historical College Age Population (2000-2023)")
display(df_census_college_age)
```

### Forecast: Kem C. Gardner Policy Institute

The following data was obtained from: https://d36oiwf74r1rap.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/SchColAgeFS-Dec2022.pdf and converted to excel using https://www.adobe.com/acrobat/online/pdf-to-excel.html tool.

```{python}
# Table 1: Utah School-Age and College-Age Population, 2020-2060
# Note: School-age reflects population ages 5 to 17. College-age reflects population ages 18 to 24.
# Source: Kem C. Gardner Policy Institute, 2020–2060 Projections
df_gpi_state_forecast = (
    pd.read_excel(
        "data/GPI/SchColAgeFS-Dec2022.xlsx",
        sheet_name="Table 1",
        header=[51, 52],
        nrows=41,
    )
    .dropna(axis=1, how="all")
    .pipe(
        lambda d: d.set_axis(
            [
                "Year",
                "Total_Population",
                "School_Total",
                "School_Abs_Growth",
                "School_Growth_Rate",
                "School_Share",
                "College_Total",
                "College_Abs_Growth",
                "College_Growth_Rate",
                "College_Share",
            ],
            axis=1,
        )
    )
)

# Table 3: College-Age Population with Change by County, 2020 and 2060
# Note: College-age reflects population ages 18 to 24.
# Source: Kem C. Gardner Policy Institute, 2020–2060 Projections
df_gpi_county_forecast = pd.read_excel(
    "data/GPI/SchColAgeFS-Dec2022.xlsx", header=129, nrows=30
).dropna(axis=1, how="all")
```


```{python}
# Source: https://d36oiwf74r1rap.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Gardner-Policy-Institute-State-and-County-Projections-2025-2065-Data.xlsx

# List of target counties for the query
wftdm_counties = [
    "Box Elder County",
    "Weber County",
    "Davis County",
    "Salt Lake County",
    "Utah County",
]

df_gpi_projections = pd.read_excel(
    "data/GPI/Gardner-Policy-Institute-State-and-County-Projections-2025-2065-Data.xlsx",
    sheet_name="Demographic Detail",
    header=3,
    nrows=1230,
).query("Geography in @wftdm_counties")[["Geography", "Year", "Population Ages 18-24"]]

(
    df_gpi_projections.pivot(
        index="Year", columns="Geography", values="Population Ages 18-24"
    )
    .rename_axis(None, axis=1)  # Removes the "Geography" label from the columns
    .reset_index()  # Moves 'Year' from index to the first column
)
```
